indian.headline: Indian markets closed lower on broad-based selling; IT and auto sectors led the decline.
indian.lead: Indian markets closed lower on broad-based selling; IT and auto sectors led the decline.
indian.brief: Sensex fell 1.17% and Nifty 50 dropped 1.07%, with Bank Nifty down 0.78%, as weakness in IT and auto outweighed gains in metals.
why: IT sector fell 1.9%, dragging both benchmark indices lower as tech stocks faced selling pressure.
Auto sector declined 1.5%, adding to downward momentum in large-cap portfolios.
Realty weakness at 1.4% and FMCG decline of 0.9% spread the selloff across consumer and real estate segments.
Metal sector's 1.4% gain and energy's flat 0.1% move could not offset broad losses elsewhere.

drivers: IT stocks fell 1.9%, pulling heavyweight tech constituents of the Sensex lower.
Auto sector weakness of 1.5% dragged major auto manufacturers in the index down.
Banking sector lost 0.8%, slightly outperforming Bank Nifty but still pressuring mid-cap and broader Nifty constituents.
FMCG decline of 0.9% and realty drop of 1.4% weighed more on Nifty's composition than on Sensex-heavy large-caps.
Banking sector fell 0.8% as profit-taking affected PSU and private lender stocks after recent strength.
Credit quality improvements and loan growth in PSBs were offset by overall market risk-off sentiment today.

indian.narrative:
Indian equities closed on a weak note on 27 November 2026, with the Sensex sliding 1.17% and Nifty 50 dropping 1.07%, reflecting broad-based selling across technology, auto, realty, and consumer segments. Bank Nifty fell a comparatively lighter 0.78%, cushioned by recent strength in public sector bank lending and credit quality. The decline came as investors reassessed valuations after a strong 2026, despite JP Morgan's bullish call for Nifty reaching 29,000 and further rallies in 2027.

Sector performance painted a mixed picture: IT led losses with a 1.9% fall, followed by auto's 1.5% drop and realty's 1.4% decline, while metals managed a 1.4% gain on commodity strength. On the commodity front, crude oil fell sharply, with Brent crude sliding to $92.02 per barrel (down 2.74%), but gold surged, rising to $3,702 per ounce (up 4.71%). The rupee weakened to 92.98 per dollar, a 0.80% decline, amid the oil price movement and regional currency headwinds. Market watchers will be eyeing regulatory developments around the Tata Steel-APL Apollo deal and SEBI's crackdown on IPO grey market platforms as potential near-term catalysts.

us.headline: US markets close mixed as tech selloff weighs on Nasdaq while energy and financials steady the ship.
us.lead: US markets close mixed as tech selloff weighs on Nasdaq while energy and financials steady the ship.
us.brief: S&P 500 fell 0.25%, Nasdaq dropped 0.62%, but Dow gained 0.33% as sector rotation favored financials and energy over technology.
why: Tech sector weakness dragged Nasdaq lower by 0.62%, with mega-cap tech stocks under pressure amid concerns over AI investment returns, particularly at SoftBank.
Financials and energy each rose 0.7%, offsetting tech losses and lifting the Dow into positive territory despite overall market caution.
Gold surged 4.72% to $3,703/oz as investors sought safety, while crude fell 2.74% to $92.02/bbl, signaling mixed risk appetite.
Tariff uncertainty over US-India trade negotiations created headwinds for exporters, though some analysts see tech selloff bottoming soon with potential recovery ahead.
us.narrative:
US equities delivered a mixed verdict on Wednesday, 27 November 2026, with the S&P 500 sliding 0.25% and Nasdaq retreating 0.62%, weighed down by a continued technology sector rout. The Dow Jones Industrial Average managed a rare gain of 0.33%, buoyed by strength in financials and energy, each rising 0.7%. Healthcare also declined 0.6%, adding to the uneven tone. Meanwhile, gold rallied 4.72% to $3,703 per ounce as investors rotated into defensive assets, while oil fell 2.74% to $92.02 per barrel, reflecting softer risk sentiment.

The selloff in mega-cap technology stocks remains the dominant theme, with mounting concerns that massive artificial intelligence bets may not generate returns fast enough to service debt—a worry that has shadowed companies like SoftBank. Despite the gloom, some strategists argue the tech downturn should find a floor soon, potentially unlocking a significant rally. On the trade front, uncertainty surrounding US tariff proposals on Indian goods added to the day's cautious backdrop, though the rupee weakened to ₹92.98 per dollar, up 0.80%. India's semiconductor ambitions also moved into focus, with the government's second major chip investment programme signaling longer-term growth intent.
